title: Prime-field MITM prepared and probed in batches (x-only sum/difference per inversion, Montgomery batch inversion, native pricing)
hypothesis: On the registry prime instances, preparing the mitm pair table with one inversion per abscissa pair and Montgomery batch inversion, and at m = 3 computing every R +/- P_i of a chunk of abscissae from one batched inversion, lowers counted end-to-end S against the registry baseline arm (prime-abscissa + mitm) at m = 2 and m = 3, with the same table entries, the same witnesses, the same trials and the same verified logarithms. The preparation and the m = 3 candidate arithmetic are charged as measured nanoseconds at the host's nanoseconds per addition (the convention of the binary mitm-batched oracle); lookups and hit verification stay counted as for mitm.
